tags.picture_matters: Two traps. (1) The English machine-translated edition of this book (doc 6ee1e2e3e24e, p. 75) re-flows the row labels so that labels and numbers no longer line up ('Independent agricultural income 1.2.' sits on the 470.3 row) and moves stars off their numbers; use the Spanish original. (2) The values use decimal commas, so '786,3' is 786.3, not 7863, and '-0,0129' is -0.0129.

                                                   (diferencias en diferencias) tratamiento
Ingresos totales del hogar (S/.)                        786,3 *        910,5 *

Índice de Herfindahl de diversificación de ingresos (1 = diversificación completa, 0 = concentración):
Desagregando el ingreso en 17 rubros                  -0,0024        -0,0028
Desagregando el ingreso en 9 grupos                   -0,0032        -0,0037

Los ingresos nominales han sido deflactados temporal (IPC, base 2009) y espacialmente (Enaho 2014) ... Los ingresos están en soles de Lima Metropolitana del 2014.
context_needed: Peru, Haku Wiñay pilot (Escobal and Ponce, eds., GRADE 2016). Design: population centres randomly assigned to treatment in 2013 or to control (treated in 2016); baseline February 2013, follow-up August-September 2015. Column 1, 'Intención del tratamiento', is the ITT, estimated as a difference in differences after entropy balancing. Column 2, 'Impacto del tratamiento', is the effect on households that actually took part (ATET, i.e. TOT), estimated by IV with assignment of the population centre as the instrument (method: Spanish PDF pp. 49-52); 86% of households in treated centres took part (explained on p. 76, the page after the table). Units: income in 2014 Lima Metropolitan soles per year (p. 76 calls the 786,3 'soles anuales'); Herfindahl rows are index points (1 = full diversification).

rule: When ITT and TOT/ATET are printed side by side for the same outcomes, store both, each with its estimand in arm; the TOT column header may not say 'TOT' (here 'Impacto del tratamiento'), so the estimand comes from the text. With stars only, se stays null and nothing is invented. Read decimal commas as decimal points.

resolved_questions.question: The table prints no SE, t or p-value, only stars. The row fields have no place for significance, so this entry keeps the star level in note. Should stars-only significance get its own field (for example 'stars': '**' with the legend), or stay in note?
resolved_questions.resolution: Reviewer convention, 22 Nov 2026: stars go in a 'stars' field on the row, with the table's legend in 'significance_legend'. Stars are recorded only when no SE, t or p is printed.
